subject: Developer access patterns & key governance — post-call action items
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir@finledger.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: FinLedger Engineering <engineering@finledger.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: integration feasibility & auth patterns

Thanks for the call earlier — this was helpful. A quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can feed this back to our platform team:

- What we want: low-latency embeddings + a reranker for search, plus a structured-output tool-calling flow for invoice extraction.
- Primary concerns: key management across service accounts, short-lived tokens for server-to-server, and how to handle rotation without disrupting production inference.

Action items we want from Redwood:
1) An integration checklist for SDK bootstrapping and recommended auth patterns (service account vs. API key for server workloads).
2) Expected downtime/impact during key rotation and suggested approach for zero-downtime rotation.
3) Any security evidence for rotation policies (SOC2 / audit log pointers).

Can you send a concise plan (2–3 options) and a recommended default? We have a sandbox environment in two weeks; timeline would be good.

—Samir
Principal Engineering Manager
FinLedger

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@finledger.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 18:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: integration feasibility & auth patterns

Samir — thanks for the clear summary and for listing the priorities. Below is a compact post-call plan and next steps; attaching a short integration checklist and a filled security questionnaire template.

1) Quick summary of recommended patterns (TL;DR):
   - Server-to-server inference: recommended path is short-lived JWTs minted by your KMS/HSM and exchanged for Redwood-issued short TTL tokens (recommended TTL 15–60 min) for production. This avoids long-lived API keys in prod while preserving simple rotation.
   - Non-prod / dev: scoped API keys tied to a sandbox project; rotate monthly and restrict by origin/IP if possible.
   - Service accounts: use a dedicated service principal per environment (sandbox, staging, prod) and bind least-privilege roles.

2) Key rotation approaches (3 options):
   A) Rolling keys with dual-acceptance: Redwood accepts both new and old tokens for a 12-hour window. You rotate at T0, mint new keys, update clients, then retire old keys. Minimal impact but requires client-side deploy coordination.
   B) Token exchange (recommended for prod): Your KMS mints JWT -> exchange endpoint returns short-lived Redwood token. No client changes on rotation; only the exchange credentials rotate.
   C) API-key split with gradual cutover: create new key, update half the fleet (canary), monitor, then cut. Works when exchange infrastructure is not available.

3) Impact during rotation:
   - Option B (token exchange) gives near-zero downtime for inference if exchange is highly available.
   - Option A can cause transient auth failures during client rollout; we recommend staging a canary first.

4) Evidence & compliance:
   - We provide audit logs for token issuance/validation (retained per your contract), and our SOC2 attestation (redacted) is available under NDA. The attached spreadsheet includes the evidence mapping for common questions.

Next steps / asks from FinLedger:
- Confirm which option (A/B/C) you want us to prototype in the sandbox.
- Provide the service-account naming convention you prefer so we can preconfigure RBAC entries in the sandbox.
- Confirm a 2-hour window for a handshake test during your sandbox kickoff (we suggested 2027-04-26).

Attached: redwood-sdk-integration-checklist.pdf; finledger-security-questions-answered.xlsx

Cheers,
Priya Natarajan
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: integration feasibility & auth patterns

Adding a few implementation details from runtime/SDK perspective — Samir, this should help the engineering team scope the sandbox work: 

- SDK bootstrapping: we have an init call that accepts either an API key or a short-lived token. For token exchange flows we recommend using our /token/exchange endpoint which validates incoming JWTs issued by your KMS and returns a scoped token (60m TTL by default).
- Structured output/tool-calling: the SDK includes a schema-validator hook (JSON Schema) to fail-fast on invalid tool payloads. We can include recommended schema examples for invoice extraction in the checklist.
- Embeddings/reranker routing: for low-latency search we recommend colocating embedding calls to the same region + enabling prefix caching on your indexer. Use model routing rules to direct high-throughput inference to dedicated pools (we can pre-provision for the sandbox).
- Rotation safety: implement a short backoff/retry with a token-refresh on 401s. The SDK exposes a token-refresh hook so you can centralize exchange logic and avoid token thrash.

I'll attach a tiny sample (in the checklist PDF) showing a token-exchange curl snippet and a minimal Node example.

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Samir Shah <samir@finledger.com>

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. We discussed briefly and prefer Option B (token exchange) for prod and Option C for sandbox to keep things simple initially. Confirming the sandbox kickoff window on 2027-04-26 10:00-12:00 PST works for our team.

A couple quick clarifications before the handoff:
- Can you include a short example of how rotation is audited (what fields show up in Redwood audit logs)?
- For the exchange flow, who holds the private key for signing JWTs — our KMS or Redwood's? We plan to keep private keys in our KMS (HashiCorp Vault).

If you can add those two bullets to the checklist and upload a new copy to the Drive link, we can lock in the sandbox and send invites.

—Samir
Principal Engineering Manager
FinLedger
